locator.section: 8.2 Product stability -- Charge competition in OE(+.) decompositions: Stevenson's Rule

evidence.curator_note: Eq 8.3 row 2, first branch (unlabeled arrow). Cleavage of the C-C bond between the propyl group and the O-CH2 carbon, with the charge migrating to the propyl fragment giving C3H7+ (4%) and the neutral methoxymethyl radical .CH2-O-CH3 as complement; printed IE(C3H7.)=8.1 eV. This charge-migration (inductive) channel is minor relative to the alpha-cleavage branch 8.3d that dominates the competition (100%). Book draws 0 arcs (summary equation); the flow is reconstructed as a heterolytic C3-C4 cleavage (both sigma electrons of bond 3-4 to C4, propyl departs as C3H7+) followed by a one-electron shift from the incipient carbanion carbon C4 to the adjacent O5, quenching the oxygen radical cation and leaving the odd electron on the methoxymethyl carbon. LOCALIZATION at the ether oxygen (n-ionization) as in 8.3a/b; the page prints (+.) over the C3H7-CH2 region.

Cross-linked MOD rule IMS_8_3_alpha (equation 8.3, cleaves the C-C bond). It cleaves the correct C-C bond and does emit a C3H7+ fragment, but it ALSO forms the CH2=O(+) double bond (the alpha product) and emits the oxocarbenium as a second cation, so its RHS carries charge +2 -- it is charge-non-conserving and conflates this 4% inductive C3H7+ branch with the 100% alpha branch (8.3d). In the true inductive channel the methoxymethyl fragment is a neutral radical with a C-O single bond, not the oxocarbenium. Dropped by the conservation guardrail. See rule_mismatches.

Book prints '4%' relative abundance under C3H7+. observed_mz 43.0542 is the curator-computed electron-mass-corrected monoisotopic m/z of C3H7+; the page prints only the % abundance and the fragment IE (8.1 eV), no m/z.
